title: Bounded execution of a conditional
statement: Fix a program environment, resource limits, and execution depth. Let $c$ be a safe condition in an initial state $\sigma$, and let $s_1,s_2$ be statements. Suppose that if $c$ holds, then $s_1$ can execute from $\sigma$ with cost at most $T'$ to a state satisfying $Q$, and if $c$ does not hold, then $s_2$ can do so. If $\mathrm{cost}(c)+1+T'\le T$, the conditional statement executes from $\sigma$ with cost at most $T$ to a state satisfying $Q$.
hypotheses_covered: The condition $c$ is safe in the initial state $\sigma$
If $c$ holds in $\sigma$, the true branch has an execution of cost at most $T'$ ending in a state satisfying $Q$
If $c$ does not hold in $\sigma$, the false branch has an execution of cost at most $T'$ ending in a state satisfying $Q$
